display.title: The Invisible Aleph: The Young Rebbe Rayatz and His Teacher, the Radatz
display.summary_short: Why do the Torah and every brachah begin with a Beis? Uncle Yossi hunts for the invisible Aleph and tells how the young Rebbe Rayatz learned to think before saying 'Baruch Atah'.
display.summary_long: A segment from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. To the tune of 'A-hunting we will go', Uncle Yossi sets out to find a missing letter: the Torah, which we have just begun reading again, starts with a Beis in 'Bereishis', and every brachah starts with a Beis in 'Baruch'. Where did the Aleph go? Hebrew letters are also numbers, and Aleph is one, standing for Hashem Echad; like Hashem, it is invisible yet always right before us. The second word of a brachah, 'Atah', means we are speaking straight to Hashem. Then a story: ten-year-old Yosef Yitzchak, son of the Rebbe Rashab and later the Frierdiker Rebbe, watched his teacher, the Radatz, and asked why he placed his hand on his forehead before every brachah. The Radatz explained that as a boy he had been brought to the Tzemach Tzedek, who told him to stop before every brachah and think before Whom he is saying 'Baruch Atah'.
display.lesson: Before you make a brachah, stop for a moment and think: you are speaking to Hashem Himself.

date.note: Cut from episode 347 (filename date 18 Oct 1988), just after the Torah reading restarted from Bereishis; re-aired in episodes 375 and 474.
